scope: Modern competitive fencing: en garde, footwork, lunge, advance-lunge and fleche.
status: Literature reference catalog; not labeled training examples or validated automatic technique thresholds.

interpretation.angle_convention: FenceCoach measures the 2D included joint angle: a straight leg is approximately 180 degrees. Papers often report anatomical flexion from approximately zero. Subtracting from 180 does not correct 2D projection, joint-model, or movement-phase differences.
interpretation.speed_convention: Blade velocity, whole-body center-of-mass velocity, hip-proxy velocity and normalized torso/s are different quantities.
comparison_requirements: compatible angle convention and camera geometry
matched target distance and intended action
matching measured landmark or body model and units

sources.quality_note: Table labels time as ms but gives decimal seconds. Means below use the explicit discussion values in milliseconds; no SD conversion stored.

references.guidance: Introductory en garde aligns the feet approximately perpendicular with knees over their toes. A simple lunge combines weapon-arm extension and rear-leg push; the illustrated finish has a bent front leg and extended rear leg. Advance initiates with the front foot; retreat with the rear foot.
references.application: Explain the conventional beginner drill. A 90-degree illustration is not a validated tolerance band or a requirement for every bout action. Do not infer frontal alignment from a side camera alone.

references.guidance: In the simple foil attack, arm straightening while threatening valid target precedes initiation of the lunge or fleche.
references.application: Compare arm-motion onset with front-foot launch for an identified simple foil drill. An elbow angle at peak alone cannot establish this ordering or award priority.

references.guidance: The fleche and forward movement with the rear foot completely passing the front foot are forbidden in sabre.
references.application: Do not transfer epee fleche benchmarks or crossing-foot drills to sabre.

references.protocol: Natural stance averaged over three measurements; mean athlete height 176.2 cm.
references.application: Useful evidence of a measurable individual starting stance, not a prescribed 41 cm stance for every athlete. FenceCoach ankle-center stance/torso ratio is not the same measurement.

references.protocol: Short/long target distances 145%/155% of athlete height; force-derived CoM velocity; front foot-off defines t0.
references.application: Match distance and task. This is neither sword-tip speed nor FenceCoach recovery hip speed.

references.protocol: Target at 1.5 times height from rear toes; 30 x 30 cm chest-height target; fastest of three successful trials per condition; 500 Hz 3D motion capture; front toe-off to front heel contact.
references.application: Protocol-specific reference means, not ideal knee targets. Current 2D included peak-frame angles do not directly match anatomical peak flexion over a 3D phase.

references.protocol: Propulsive lunge; rear-leg 3D kinematics, sword kinematics and kinetics.
references.application: Motivates coordinated rear hip-knee-ankle propulsion. Do not compare with hip-proxy speed or classify an individual as novice from one velocity.

references.guidance: In maximum-effort lunges, elite participants had higher horizontal body velocity and rear-leg ground force; rear-knee power, moment and range of motion were associated with these outputs.
references.application: Prioritize rear-leg propulsion and sequencing when investigating slow lunges. A video joint angle does not measure force or prove a strength deficit.

references.protocol: 120 Hz 3D kinematics and force measurements; movements from en garde.
references.application: Movement-specific examples only. Two athletes cannot define normal speed or a good/bad threshold. Resultant velocity is not horizontal hip velocity.

references.metric: attack movement time excluding reaction time
references.protocol: Coach-triggered visual-response attacks ending with successful touch on coach's trunk.
references.application: Do not compare to onset-to-stance-peak or recovery intervals. Touch detection and compatible movement-onset events are required.
